paper.title_en: Selection--Clustering Coupling and Pair-Midpoint Anisotropy from Observer Motion
paper.abstract_en: Observer motion couples source selection, clustering, and estimator normalization in cosmological pair statistics. Existing calculations distinguish the source-count dipole from the modulation of clustering, including selection-dependent bias. We develop an observable-level formulation that retains arbitrary marked pair kernels, nonfactorizable pair inclusion, and explicit reference measures. Its independent-selection limit expresses the residual as a covariance of the selection score with pair excess; in a rank-one bias model this is the logarithmic response of the selected mean bias and recovers the corresponding bias-derivative description. Two populations can have the same count-dipole coefficient and isotropic correlation but opposite two-point boost responses. We show that local division by endpoint means is not equivalent to a scalar normalization of integrated pair counts, and derive the contact terms and self-pair subtraction required for discrete harmonic estimators. Exchange symmetry permits pair-midpoint anisotropy but forbids an ordinary unordered same-tracer separation dipole. The known neighboring-multipole templates are recovered, with explicit conditions for velocity--selection degeneracy and its uncertainty cost. Finite-boost forward models independently test the response, including a nonfactorizable retained-pair example. The result is a common framework for bias-response limits, general pair selection, normalization, and covariance conventions; the numerical illustrations are controlled models rather than survey forecasts. An observational route is specified through radio and infrared catalog selections, full-pipeline response calibration, and common-velocity consistency tests.
